title: Construction of normalized coefficient transport data and its system constraints
statement: Fix l,E and a family W of schemes with l invertible. There exists Transport l E W [def-pur-completed-coefficient-family-transport-models] satisfying ExpressionSystemLaw and ExpressionSystemStructuralLaw [def-pur-completed-coefficient-system-transport]. Its tensor, pullback and adjunction fields retain all quotient-system and actual-unit normalizations. This assertion concerns construction on the common normalized systems; it does not assert simultaneous substitution or structural coherence of the recursively defined constant-side expression comparison.

proof.text: Write $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $K_{R,n}=K\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{W,n}$. Apply the constant/completed equivalence with the Noetherian DVR $A$ and ideal $(t)$. It gives flatness of $R_W$ over $\underline A_W$, $R_W/t^nR_W=B_{W,n}$, compatible finite comparisons $c_{K,n}:U_WK\otimes^L_{\underline A_W}B_{W,n}\simeq K_{R,n}$, and preservation of the total limits of these strict reduction systems. Its last paragraph, together with the reflector statement, gives a natural isomorphism $d_K:U_WC_W^RK\simeq C_W^AU_WK$ characterized by $d_K\,U_W\eta_K^R=\eta^A_{U_WK}$. Thus this comparison identifies the actual units on every ambient $R_W$-object, before any assumption that $K$ is complete. The equivalence restricts to the complete full subcategories.

source.place: Tags 099I (lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence) and 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul); finite-quotient version: proetale.tex, Tag 099M

proof.text: Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $P,Q$ of $M,N$, and $P_H$ of $H$. The resolution theorem applies to arbitrary unbounded module-sheaf complexes. By flat scalar restriction, $U_WP,U_WQ$ are flat-term K-flat over $\underline A_W$. By the total-tensor theorem their direct-sum total tensor computes $U_WM\otimes^L_{\underline A_W}U_WN$ and is again flat-term K-flat. The analogous assertion over $R_W$ computes $M\otimes^L_{R_W}N$. Derived ringed pullback and coefficient extension preserve these good representatives, so finite reductions and pullbacks below are computed on these same complexes. In particular no truncation or finite Tor-amplitude is used.

For every $n$, scalar-extension tensor compatibility and $c_{M,n},c_{N,n}$ give the isomorphism
$$\theta_n:(U_WM\otimes^L_{\underline A_W}U_WN)\otimes^L_{\underline A_W}B_{W,n}\simeq M_{R,n}\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_{R,n}.$$
On the representatives of step 2 its local pure-tensor formula is $(p\otimes q)\otimes s\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes(q\otimes s)$. The inverse sends $(p\otimes a)\otimes(q\otimes b)$ to $(p\otimes q)\otimes ab$, using the finite comparisons $c$. Balancing is exactly the scalar-extension tensor comparison; it is valid sheafwise because $R_W/t^nR_W=B_{W,n}$. For a quotient $q_{m,n}:B_{W,m}\to B_{W,n}$, either order of applying this formula and the transition sends $(p\otimes q)\otimes s$ to $(p\otimes1)\otimes(q\otimes q_{m,n}(s))$. Thus these are maps and inverse maps of the whole strict quotient complexes, not independently chosen finite-level arrows.

source.place: Tag 099I with the finite-quotient comparisons; sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 07A4, applied to scalar extension

proof.text:
Take total derived limit of $\theta_\bullet^{-1}$. The definition of completed tensor identifies its source with $U_W(M\widehat\otimes_RN)$; the quotient-completion formula identifies its target with $C_W^A(U_WM\otimes^L_{\underline A_W}U_WN)$. This is $a_{M,N}$. It is natural, and independent of representatives by the well-definedness theorem for the quotient operations and the canonical finite comparisons. If $\mu:U_WM\otimes^L_{\underline A_W}U_WN\to U_W(M\otimes^L_{R_W}N)$ is the balancing map, the same formula with $s=1$ gives
$$a_{M,N}\,U_W(\eta^R_{M\otimes^L_RN})\,\mu=\eta^A_{U_WM\otimes^L_AU_WN},$$
where the source of $a$ is identified with completion of the ordinary $R$-tensor by the reduction-tower comparison. This also fixes its unit normalization, rather than choosing an arbitrary isomorphism between its endpoints.

source.place: Tags 099I and 0A0E; proetale.tex, Tag 099M; quotient tensor construction of def-pur-integral-derived-operations

proof.text:
Put $Q_R=Lf_R^*$ and $Q_A=f^{-1}$. The pullback clause of the constant/completed equivalence identifies the finite reductions of $U_XQ_RH$ with $Q_A(U_YH\otimes^L_A B_{Y,n})$. It says explicitly that the finite reduction of the scalar-unit map $\tau_H:Q_AU_YH\to U_XQ_RH$ is the inverse of this identification. On a good representative it is $x\mapsto1\otimes x$; quotient maps commute with it. Apply total derived limit to this comparison of strict systems. The left side is $C_X^AQ_AU_YH$, and the right side is $U_XC_X^RQ_RH=U_X\widehat f_R^*H$: the latter equality follows by applying ringed pullback/tensor compatibility to the reductions of $Q_RH$, exactly the tower defining the completed pullback. This defines the natural isomorphism $b_H$ and yields the actual equation
$$b_H\,\eta^A_{Q_AU_YH}=U_X(\eta^R_{Q_RH})\,\tau_H.$$
This follows on the augmented strict towers before total limit.

For complete inputs their coherent reduction systems are normalized: successive derived reductions of a K-flat representative reassociate to its direct reduction, with the ordinary quotient transitions. The constant coefficient reductions identify with the same systems by $c_{K,n}$. Normalized effectivity recovers each input from its system by the actual coherent counit. Apply the completed-operation substitution theorem to these systems. Every finite expression in tensor, pullback and the coefficient unit is represented by its whole system expression, with comparisons induced by these counits. Since steps 3 and 5 constructed their maps on precisely these systems, their iterates are the substitution comparisons of that theorem. For the constant-coefficient expression, use the same systems via $c$ and the quotient-completion formula, so its comparison is fixed by the same representatives and units. The coefficient unit on each side is reconstructed from $(B_{W,n})_n$; on the constant side this is $C_W^A(\underline A_W)$.

source.place: Blueprint lem-fix-operation-reduction.proof.md, final paragraph; normalized quotient-system realization of its tensor/pullback clauses

proof.text: Check the structural maps on the common whole-system representatives of step 6. Tensor associativity is $(p\otimes q)\otimes r\mapsto p\otimes(q\otimes r)$; the two unitors multiply the coefficient in $B_{W,n}$; symmetry sends $p\otimes q$ to $(-1)^{|p||q|}q\otimes p$. Reassociation in $\theta$ changes no degree and commutes with each of these formulas. Finite pullback distributes over tensor by the canonical map of the ringed pullback/tensor theorem. Inserting the scalar unit before or after that map sends both tensor factors to $1\otimes(-)$. For successive pullbacks the two insertions give $1\otimes(1\otimes x)$, identified with $1\otimes x$ by scalar multiplication. These formulas commute with every coefficient quotient, so they are identities of chain maps of systems; the total differentials and symmetry use the same Koszul signs. Applying the system localization and total-limit functors, with the substitution comparisons, gives the asserted associator, unitor, symmetry, tensor/pullback and pullback-composition compatibilities. Preservation of the completion units is already the augmented-system calculation in steps 1, 4 and 5.

source.place: Blueprint lem-fix-operation-reduction.proof.md, first and final paragraphs; sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 07A4, proof by total-complex maps

proof.text:
The completed-coefficient pushforward comparison supplies the specified $\kappa:U_YF_R\simeq F_AU_X$, with the K-injective derived-composition normalization, and says that $F_R$ preserves complete objects and corresponds to $F_A$ on them. The ringed coefficient-restriction counit lemma applies to the constant algebra sheaves $\underline A_W\to R_W$ and the structural map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$: these are exactly the coefficient maps here. With this same $\kappa$ and the scalar-unit $\tau$ of step 5, it gives
$$U_X\varepsilon_{R,M}\,\tau_{F_RM}=\varepsilon_{A,U_XM}\,Q_A(\kappa_M).$$
This is the ordinary counit identity for arbitrary ambient $M$. In particular its hypotheses impose neither a bound nor constructibility. The auxiliary distinct prime in the pushforward node can be chosen arbitrarily distinct from $\ell$; it imposes no condition on the schemes or coefficients used in its conclusion.

source.place: Tag 099K, completeness of direct image; ordinary derived-composition-normalized coefficient restriction counit in lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-restriction-counit

proof.text:
Use the completed adjunctions specified by the reflector Hom bijections. The Koszul reflector theorem supplies those bijections for every source and complete target. The direct-image preservation from step 8 verifies the hypothesis needed to restrict the right adjoints. The reflector-adjunction formula therefore applies to $Q_R\dashv F_R$ and $Q_A\dashv F_A$. In the present notation it says
$$\varepsilon^c_{R,M}\,\eta^R_{Q_RF_RM}=\varepsilon_{R,M},\qquad
\varepsilon^c_{A,U_XM}\,\eta^A_{Q_AF_AU_XM}=\varepsilon_{A,U_XM}.$$
These fix the two counits by their respective ordinary counits, and precomposition with $\eta^A_Z$ is injective on maps to any complete constant-coefficient target.

source.place: Tag 099K, displayed Hom bijection in its proof, with the actual completion units of Tag 0A0E

proof.text:
For complete $M$, compare the two maps in the desired equality after precomposition with $\eta^A_{Q_AU_YF_RM}$. For the left route, the unit equation of step 5 and the first equation of step 9 give
$$U_X\varepsilon^c_{R,M}\,b_{F_RM}\,\eta^A_{Q_AU_YF_RM}=U_X\varepsilon_{R,M}\,\tau_{F_RM}.$$
For the right route, naturality of $\eta^A$ and the second equation of step 9 give
$$\varepsilon^c_{A,U_XM}\,\widehat f_A^*(\kappa_M)\,\eta^A_{Q_AU_YF_RM}=\varepsilon_{A,U_XM}\,Q_A(\kappa_M).$$
Step 8 identifies these two ordinary composites. Since $U_XM$ is complete by the equivalence, injectivity of precomposition with that very completion unit proves the required equality of completed counits. This is a reflector argument about actual morphisms, not a claim that finite reductions detect equality.

source.place: Tag 099K, proof; elementary cancellation through its completion-reflector Hom bijection

proof.text:
Finally check the whole Hom bijection, hence also the units. For complete $H,M$ and $s:H\to F_RM$, the inverse completed $R$-adjunction sends $s$ to $t=\varepsilon^c_{R,M}\,\widehat f_R^*(s)$. Transport the right Hom arrow to $s_A=\kappa_M\,U_Ys$. Its inverse completed $A$-adjunct is
$$\varepsilon^c_{A,U_XM}\,\widehat f_A^*(s_A)
=U_X\varepsilon^c_{R,M}\,b_{F_RM}\,\widehat f_A^*(U_Ys)
=U_Xt\,b_H,$$
by step 10 and naturality of $b$. This proves equality of the inverse bijections, so also of the bijections. These are bijections on the transported Hom sets because $U$ is fully faithful on complete objects and $\kappa,b$ are isomorphisms. Taking $M=\widehat f_R^*H$ and the identity left Hom arrow shows that the completed unit is carried to the completed unit under $b,\kappa$. Thus the specified completed adjunctions, with all their units and counits, agree. Every calculation used unbounded K-flat models, strict-system functors or the reflector bijection, so no additional finiteness hypothesis has entered.
